text:
B: Hi, can you hear me okay?
A: Yes, I can hear you. Good afternoon. I am Tomasz.
B: Isaac. Nice to meet you. Erm, are you the last one for me? I think you are.
A: I think so, yes. Also for me. It is a long afternoon.
B: Ha, yeah, it is. Kind of fun though. Where are you based?
A: Crawley. Near Gatwick.
B: Oh, nice, not that far from me. I'm in Croydon, Thornton Heath. Same train line, basically, the Southern one. Which is always late.
A: Yes. I do not take the train so much now. I drive, or I walk.
B: Fair enough. What do you do, if you don't mind me asking?
A: I was a civil engineer, drainage and highways. Now I am looking for work. The company made people redundant last year.
B: Oh, sorry, that's rubbish. Is it hard, like, finding stuff?
A: It is slow. I keep a spreadsheet of every application. The date, the company, the reply. Mostly no reply.
B: Nah, that's literally what I do. I've got a spreadsheet for internships, all the deadlines. Spring weeks, summer stuff. I'm doing Economics at City, so it's mainly banks and consultancies. Half of them don't reply either, so, you know, it's not just you.
A: Ha. Then we are in the same club.
B: Yeah, the no-reply club.
A: You are young. You will get something. You seem organised.
B: Erm, I try. I kind of panic otherwise, to be honest. Like, I run a little tutoring service as well, so I have to keep track of that too. Well, I say service, it's like three students. Sorry, I'm making it sound bigger than it is.
A: Three students is good. To explain something to another person, it is a real skill. I did this with the junior engineers. Some of them, I explained the same thing five times.
B: Five times? And you didn't get annoyed?
A: No. The fifth time, usually they understand. And then they explain it to the next one.
B: That's nice, actually. I'll remember that when my Year 11 kid asks about supply and demand again.
A: May I ask, you have the trainers in boxes in your photo. You collect them?
B: Kind of. I buy limited ones and sell them on. Some I keep. The boxes keep them clean, otherwise they lose value.
A: Very sensible. Like an engineer. You protect the asset.
B: Ha, protect the asset. I'm gonna tell my dad that, he thinks it's a waste of shelf space.
A: Fathers always think this. My son had a motorbike magazine collection. I said the same.
B: Ha. Erm, I saw the crucifix behind you as well. Are you, like, a churchgoer?
A: Yes, Catholic. The Polish Mass, most Sundays. And you?
B: Methodist, sort of. My mum goes every week. I go Christmas, Easter, when my nan's down. You kind of remind me of some of the uncles at our church, actually. In a good way, I mean.
A: Ha. I will take this as a compliment.
B: It is, it is. They're the ones who always ask how uni's going and actually listen. My granddad's been ill recently, so they've been, erm, really good with the family, to be fair.
A: I am sorry about your grandfather. I hope he gets better. A church family, it helps in these times.
B: Yeah. Thanks. It does, yeah.
A: And your studies, the economics. What will you do when you finish, if the bank—
